blocks.prompt: 9 Solve the following trigonometric equation: \(\sin 2x - \sqrt{3}\cos x = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
Is equation mein do alag angles hain: \(2x\) aur \(x\). Jab tak angle ek na ho, hum factor nahin nikal sakte.
Is liye double-angle formula \(\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x\) lagayenge; phir \(\cos x\) common nikal aayega.
Find kya karna hai? Principal solutions aur general solution.
Plan: formula, factorise, \(\cos x = 0\) aur \(\sin x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) hal karo, families jodo.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\sin 2x - \sqrt{3}\cos x = 0\).
Maloom karna: principal solutions aur general solution.
Tareeqa: double-angle formula se sab kuch angle \(x\) mein laayenge, phir factorise karenge.

Double-angle formula lagayein
\[2\sin x\cos x - \sqrt{3}\cos x = 0\]
Kyun: \(\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x\). Ab dono terms ek hi angle \(x\) mein hain aur dono mein \(\cos x\) hai.

Factorise karein
\[\cos x\left(2\sin x - \sqrt{3}\right) = 0\]
\[\cos x = 0\ \text{ or }\ \sin x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\cos x\) common nikala; product zero to koi ek factor zero.
Dhyan dein: \(\cos x\) se divide mat kijiye, warna \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) aur \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) gum ho jayenge.

Jab \(\cos x = 0\)
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\]
\([0, 2\pi]\) mein. Dono mein \(\pi\) ka farq hai, is liye aam taur par \(x = \frac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\).
Kyun: cosine (x-coordinate) circle ke sab se upar aur sab se neeche wale points par zero hota hai, jo aadhe chakkar ke faasle par hain.

Jab \(\sin x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\)
Sine positive: quadrant I aur II, reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\).
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
\[x = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: table se \(\sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\); quadrant II ka angle \(\pi - \alpha\).

General solution
\[\left\{\dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{2\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Kyun: dono factors ki families ka union. Pehli family \(n\pi\) wali hai (cosine ke do zero aadhe chakkar ke faasle par), baqi do \(2n\pi\) wali (sine ka period \(2\pi\)).

Tasdeeq
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}:\ \sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \sqrt{3}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 0\]
Kyun: \(2x = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) aur \(\sin\frac{2\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Isi tarah \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) par \(\sin\pi - \sqrt{3}\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0 - 0 = 0\).
blocks.final_answer: Principal solutions \([0, 2\pi]\) mein: \(x = \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{2\pi}{3}, \frac{3\pi}{2}\). General solution: \(\left\{\frac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\right\}\) \(\cup\) \(\left\{\frac{\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\}\) \(\cup\) \(\left\{\frac{2\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab mein Exercise 10.1 ke jawab chhape hue nahin hain. Is page ka har jawab hamara apna hai: qadam ba qadam hal kiya gaya, computer algebra system (sympy) se alag se check kiya gaya, aur ek solution book se bhi milaya gaya. Kitab ke examples ki tarah hum principal solutions \([0, 2\pi]\) mein aur general solution sets ke union ki shakal mein dete hain. Aap apna kaam yahan wale hal se mila kar dekh sakte hain.
